memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So Moses said, 'This is what the LORD says: About midnight I will go throughout
Egypt.'" - Ex 11:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses is still standing before Pharaoh from the end of chapter 10, and now he
delivers the final word. Notice the precision: "About midnight." God names the
hour.

Notice also who is coming. Not an angel sent on an errand, not a natural
disaster rolling in. "I will go throughout Egypt." God Himself.

Through the earlier plagues, God had acted through Moses' staff and Aaron's
hand. Now, in the final judgment, He comes personally. This tells us how serious
the moment is. Egypt had asked, through Pharaoh's mouth, "Who is the LORD, that
I should obey him?" (Ex 5:2). They are about to find out.

Midnight is a fitting hour. It is the deepest darkness, when people are asleep
and defenceless. Egypt would not see this coming, though they had been warned
for months.

For us, this verse is a sober reminder that God's patience has a limit and His
warnings are real. But it also reminds us that the God who comes in judgment is
the same God who came in mercy, personally, in Jesus Christ. He did not send
someone else to save us. He came Himself (John 1:14).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there warnings from God you have been treating as background noise?
2. What does it mean to you that God came personally in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are patient, but You are also holy. Keep me from taking Your warnings
lightly, and thank You that You came Yourself to save me. Amen.
